pageCache.pageTitle: Crawley Ridge Infant School - Essential Letters and Sounds
pageCache.text:
Essential Letters and Sounds
From October 2021 our school started to embed and use a new phonics scheme, Essential Letters and Sounds.
Below we have collated as much information as possible to ensure that parents are able to continue to support their children with learning, outside of school. Of course if you would like any more information or to discuss other ways in which you can help your child learn to read then our door is always open.
Harder to Read and Spell Words
HRS words, are words that children should know even though they have not yet been taught the relevant GPCs (Grapheme Phoneme Correspondences) within these words. HRS words are common in the English language, and it is important that children can read and spell them. When teaching a new HRS, we always identify the graphemes (letters which represent the sound) within the word that make it tricky e.g they (ey is tricky). Please see the Reception and Year 1 documents which outline the order and term in which these words will be taught at Crawley Ridge Infant School.
Press the links below:
Reception Harder to Read and Spell Words
Year 1 Harder to Read and Spell Words
Reading with your child
Reading books are changed once per week. This allows your child to re-read each text several times, building their confidence and fluency. This is especially important as they begin to learn that the sounds within our language can be spelt in different ways.
For children, re-reading words and sentences that they can decode (sound out) until they are fluent (read with ease and precision) is a key part of learning to read. By reading texts several times, children have the greatest opportunity to achieve this fluency.
The texts sent home are carefully matched to the teaching taking place in school. Your child will be practising what they have been taught in school with you at home. We will only ask children to read books independently when they can decode these by themselves.
How to pronounce sounds
Reception – Phase 2
During the Autumn term, our Reception children learn phase 2 sounds. They focus on oral blending as well as sounding out and blending the 23 new grapheme-phoneme correspondences (GPCs). They will also learn 12 new harder to read and spell words (HRS). Please see the HRS section for a list of words the children will learn and when.
These Phase 2 sounds will continue to be used throughout the children’s time at Crawley Ridge Infant School. We ensure that we model pure sounds so that the children are able to blend successfully. Please see the video below so you can hear how to pronounce the “pure sounds”. Parent feedback has requested further support with sound articulation so we have included these links on our website for you. A consistent approach optimises success for the children so please let us know if you require further support with how to help your child with their phonics.

During the second half of the Autumn term and throughout the Spring Term, Reception children learn phase 3 sounds. Mad Science
***** NEW IN SPRING 2026 *****
Learning doesn't have to stop after the bell rings! Mad Science after-school programs are both educational and fun. Our hands-on, one-hour, 6-week science programs are themed around a particular area of science and include such topics as electricity, magnetism, optics, biology, and many more. Our unique approach gives children a solid scientific foundation that goes beyond the classroom. Children engage in hands-on activities, watch spectacular demos and take part in curiosity building investigations each week, delivered by our expert Mad Scientists at your child's school!
Mondays 3pm - 4pm in Amethyst classroom.

Visit the Year Group pages regularly for important information from your child's class teacher.

SEND
Class teachers continually assess children's learning and development needs. Tasks are differentiated to meet individual needs in the classroom setting.
Children with specific requirements may be registered on the Code of Practice ( CoP) for Special Educational Needs (SEN) and will be given an Individual Education Plan (IEP) that is initiated in consultation with parents, the class teacher and the Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo). An IEP is designed to enable a child to make progress towards specifc targets. All children's progress is monitored and tracked, and the IEPs are reviewed regularly to meet the requirements of the Code of Practice.
Advantage is taken of support offered by outside agencies, such as Speech Therapy, Language and Literacy Support Services, English as an Additional Language service, Educational Psychologist etc as appropriate to a child's needs and stage of development.
Parents are closely involved at all stages if a child is registered on the Code of Practice.
Our SEND Policy and SEN Information Report may be found on the Policies page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crawley Ridge Infant School - Wrap Around Care
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
5 O’clock Club – After-School Care at Crawley Ridge Infant School
5 O’clock Club is our after-school provision, offering a safe, friendly, and familiar environment for children that attend our school.
The club is run by Crawley Ridge Infant School staff and takes place on-site in the Nurture Hub and/or main school hall. Children enjoy time to play, relax, and take part in activities, with a light snack and drink provided.
Opening Times and Fees
5 O’Clock Club runs Monday to Friday during term time (excluding INSET days and school closures):
3:00pm – 4:30pm: £9.00 per session
3:00pm – 5:00pm: £12.50 per session
Only two collection times are available (4:30pm or 5:00pm).
We reserve the right to charge an additional £10 for the first 15 minutes after 4:30 or 5pm for late pick-ups, to cover staff overtime costs. Any collection after 4:45/5.15pm will incur additional charges of 50p per minute per child.
Fees are reviewed each half-term.
Who Can Attend?
If demand is high, places are offered based on the following priority criteria:
Children previously on the Graitney Club waiting list
Children attending five days a week
Children attending three or more regular sessions per week
Children attending regular weekly sessions
Can I use childcare vouchers?
We accept both government childcare vouchers and Tax-Free Childcare payments. When making payments through your provider, please select Crawley Ridge Junior School as the registered setting. All funds are automatically transferred back to Crawley Ridge Infant School.
How to Book
Bookings are made using our online Microsoft Form. Once confirmed, your booking is ongoing unless cancelled with six weeks written notice. Invoices are issued half-termly. We cannot accept bookings where payments are overdue.
The form will not close but we will remove sessions once they reach capacity.
Booking Form for Summer 2 below
Summer 2 bookings for 5 O’Clock Club will open on Monday 4th May at 12 noon.
The form below is for sessions between Monday 1st June and Thursday 16th July.
Please check your booking carefully before submitting, as sessions cannot be changed or cancelled once booked. Non-attendance will still be charged.
Sessions will be removed from the form once they are full.
Booking Form for Autumn 1 2026 below
Bookings for Autumn 1 2026 will open on Monday 25th May at 12 noon.
The form below is for sessions between Thursday 3rd September and Friday 16th October.
Please check your booking carefully before submitting, as sessions cannot be changed or cancelled once booked. Non-attendance will still be charged.
New Reception children will have a staggered start at the beginning of term. Because of this, new Reception children cannot book 5 O’Clock Club sessions before Friday 11th September 2026. This is the earliest date available for new Reception children, as it is their first full day in school.
Sessions will be removed from the form once they are full.
Policies and Expectations
5 O’Clock Club follows the Crawley Ridge Infant School and TAMAT policies, including those on behaviour, safeguarding, data protection, and complaints. All children are expected to follow the school’s behaviour expectations.
A full list of club-specific and school-wide policies is available on request.
